sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Patroklos** ​(*patroclus*) ‌— Warrior, ‌Companion ​of ​Achilles · ​Father's ​glory ​— ‌belongs to ​the ​Greek ‌tradition, where ​it ‌is ​catalogued ‌under the ​domain ​"Warrior, ​Companion of ​Achilles". ​The ‌name ​means "Father's ‌glory".

​**Patroklos** ‌is warrior, ​companion ‌of ​achilles. ‌The name ​means ​"Father's ‌glory" and ‌belongs ‌to ​the ​greek tradition.

‌PuniCodex ​restores ​the name ‌as ​**Patroklos** ​and ‌serves its ​temple ‌at ​[its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/patroclus/). The ​original ​preserves ‌one prosodic ‌feature ​— ‌stress ​or vowel ​length ‌— ‌rather than ‌both, ‌which ​places ‌the name ​in ​Tier ​2. The ‌plain ​ASCII ​form ​*patroclus* survives ‌as ​a ​modern convenience ​imposed ‌by ​the ‌early domain-name ​system; ‌the ​restoration, not ‌the ‌fallback, ​is ​the form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in Greek ​as ​**Πάτροκλος**. Etymologically ​it ​means "Father's ​glory".

‌The ASCII ​form ​*patroclus* survives ‌only because ​the ‌early domain-name ​system ‌could not ​carry ​diacritics; it ​is ​a technological ​compromise, ‌not an ​ancient ‌spelling. The ​Unicode ‌restoration **Patroklos** ​recovers ‌the full ​diacritic ‌detail of ​the ​scholarly transliteration ‌directly in ‌the ‌address bar. ​The ​original preserves ‌one ​prosodic feature ​— ‌stress or ​vowel ​length — ‌rather ​than both, ‌which ​places the ​name ​in Tier ​2.

‌The letter-by-letter ‌transformation ​runs:

- ‌**p** ​→ **P** ​— Same
‌- ‌**a** → ‌**a** ‌— Same
​- ‌**t** → ​**t** ​— Same
​- ‌**r** → ​**r** ​— Same
​- ‌**o** → ​**o** ​— Same
​- ‌**c** → ​**k** ‌— Kappa
​- **l** ‌→ ​**l** — ‌Same
‌- **u** ​→ ​**o** — ​Omicron
​- **s** ‌→ ‌**s** — ​Same

sections.purpose: IPA reconstruction, phoneme breakdown, approximation, kin forms.
sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/patroclus/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**patroclus** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Patroklos.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"patroclus" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Patroklos".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"patroclus" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Patroklos" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Patroklos was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Patroklos ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Patroklos ‌place ​warrior, companion ​of ​achilles at ​the ​center ‌of a ​living ​mythological world.

‌### ​Origins (Myth)

‌Patroklos ​appears ‌in greek ​tradition ​as warrior, ​companion ​of ​achilles. The ‌name's ​meaning, "Father's ‌glory", ​shapes ‌the narratives ​told ‌about this ​figure.

‌### ​Worship and ​Memory ‌(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ‌later tradition-keepers ​preserved ​Patroklos ‌in ritual, ​text, ​and iconography, ‌ensuring ​the ​name survived ‌into ​the modern ‌scholarly ​record.

​The myths ​of ​Patroklos survive ‌in ‌fragments, ​summaries, and ‌later ​retellings. Each ​version ‌reflects the ‌interests ‌of ‌its tellers ​— ‌poets, priests, ​philosophers, ​and ​scholars. The ‌PuniCodex ​entry does ​not ​privilege ‌a single ​version; ​it gathers ​the ‌attestations ​so that ‌readers ​can compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Patroklos ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Patroklos ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Greek ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Πάτροκλος, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​warrior ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Patroklos is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea of ​warrior, ​Companion ‌of ​Achilles in ​the ‌mind ​and ‌to ​ask what ‌of ​it ​endures. ​The name ​means ​"Father's ‌glory" ​— and ‌a ​name ‌that ​carries its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly ​invites meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. ​The tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name ​as warrior, ‌Companion ​of ​Achilles ‌· Father's ​glory.

‌Sit ​with ​the restored ​form ​— ‌Patroklos ‌— and ​the ‌diacritics ​themselves ​become ‌the practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ​a small ‌act ​of ​attention, ​a refusal ‌to ​let ​the ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*patroclus* ​stand ​in for ‌the ​whole. ‌What ​the ‌tradition preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
